resource.name: aws_redshift_endpoint_access
resource.description: Creates a new Amazon Redshift endpoint access.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of private endpoint access for Amazon Redshift clusters, facilitating secure connectivity from VPCs to Redshift without traversing the public internet. Common use cases include configuring Redshift for private network access, integrating analytics workloads with VPC-based applications, and enhancing data security in compliance-sensitive environments. Users can define key settings such as VPC IDs, subnet configurations, and security group rules to tailor network access and ensure seamless integration with their cloud infrastructure.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` resource, showcasing how to create an endpoint access for a Redshift cluster using the `clusterIdentifier`, `endpointName`, and `subnetGroupName` arguments. It illustrates how to link the endpoint to an existing Redshift cluster and subnet group for enabling external access.

arguments.name: cluster_identifier
arguments.llm_summary: The `cluster_identifier` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon Redshift cluster for which endpoint access is being configured. By setting this required value, users define the target cluster to associate with the custom endpoint, enabling connectivity and access management for applications or services interacting with the cluster.

arguments.name: endpoint_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `endpoint_name` argument specifies the unique name of the Redshift-managed VPC endpoint being created or accessed, allowing users to define a custom identifier for the endpoint. Setting this argument ensures the endpoint is easily identifiable and can be referenced for secure connectivity between Redshift clusters and client applications within a VPC.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` resource represents the unique identifier of the Redshift endpoint access configuration. While not required, it is typically used to reference or manage the resource within Terraform, enabling users to track and interact with the endpoint access instance programmatically.

arguments.name: resource_owner
arguments.llm_summary: The `resource_owner` argument in the `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` resource allows users to specify the AWS account ID that owns the Redshift-managed VPC endpoint being accessed. By defining this argument, users can control cross-account access to the endpoint, enabling configurations for shared resources or multi-account architectures.

arguments.name: subnet_group_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_group_name` argument in the `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` resource specifies the name of the Redshift subnet group to associate with the endpoint access. By defining this argument, users control the network configuration for the endpoint, ensuring it is provisioned within the designated subnets to enable secure and optimized connectivity to the Redshift cluster.

arguments.name: vpc_security_group_ids
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_security_group_ids` argument for the `aws_redshift_endpoint_access` resource allows users to specify a set of VPC security group IDs to control network access to the Redshift-managed VPC endpoint. By configuring this argument, users can define security rules that govern inbound and outbound traffic, ensuring secure connectivity and compliance with organizational network policies.

attributes.name: address
attributes.description: The DNS address of the endpoint.

attributes.name: port
attributes.description: The port number on which the cluster accepts incoming connections.
